paraphrase: Define a set of security policies and have management approve them.
Publish the policies and have personnel and relevant outside parties acknowledge them.
Review each policy at planned intervals and after significant change.
Define security roles and their responsibilities.
Allocate each security role to a named, current person.
Identify duties that conflict and require them to be separated.
Show through system roles or approvals that different people perform each side of a conflicting pair.
Document compensating measures where separation is not feasible.
Require, in a document personnel receive, that staff follow security policies and procedures.
Have managers brief or require their teams to comply, with records.
Keep a current list of relevant authorities and verify it regularly.
Define who may contact authorities and within what timelines for reportable events.
Record which specialist forums and professional groups the organization joins.
Take part actively and circulate what is learned.
Define the threat information sources and how they are analyzed for relevance.
Produce threat intelligence outputs in the period.
Act on threat intelligence, for example by updating the risk register or blocking rules.
Require security requirements and risks to be addressed at set stages of every project, whatever its type.
Keep project records showing a security assessment or requirements sign-off.
Maintain an inventory of information and associated assets in scope.
Assign an owner to every inventory entry.
Keep the inventory updated and matching live assets.
Set rules for acceptable and prohibited use of information and assets.
Document how information is handled at each classification level.
Have users acknowledge the rules.
Require return of all organizational assets on leaving or on change of role, contract or agreement.
Check returned assets against the inventory.
Define classification levels and the criteria for assigning them.
Assign a classification to information assets.
Define how each classification level is marked, consistent with the scheme.
Apply labels to documents, systems and media as the procedure requires.
Set rules for each transfer channel used, stating the protection required.
Cover transfers with external parties by agreements containing security terms.
Enforce the rules through technical settings on the main channels.
Set rules for physical and logical access based on business and security needs.
Apply the rules in actual access configurations.
Manage creation, change and removal of identities, each linked to one person or an owned account.
Reconcile active accounts against the HR roster so departed staff have no active identity.
Assign an owner to every service and other non-person account.
Control issuing, resetting and revoking of authentication information, verifying identity before reset.
Give users written guidance on keeping authentication information confidential.
Change default vendor credentials on installation.
Require access to be requested and approved before it is provisioned or changed.
Review access at the defined frequency and remove inappropriate access.
Remove or adjust access within the set timeframe when people leave or change role.
Define how suppliers are identified, risk-rated and selected.
Keep a register of suppliers with access to information or systems, each with a risk rating.
Complete a security due-diligence assessment before contract signature or access.
Keep a standard set of supplier security clauses, varied by supplier type or risk.
Agree security terms in contracts with high-risk suppliers.
Require ICT suppliers to pass security requirements to sub-suppliers and disclose critical components.
Assess the supply chain of key ICT suppliers, for example through sub-processor lists or component provenance.
Set how often each supplier risk tier is reviewed and what the review covers.
Review high-risk suppliers at that frequency.
Assess the security impact of material changes to supplier services.
Define how cloud services are selected, used, managed and exited, including shared responsibilities.
Keep a register of cloud services with provider assurance reviewed in the period.
Plan exit for critical cloud services, covering data return and deletion.
Document an incident management procedure covering detection through closure.
Define incident roles with named people and contact details.
Communicate the procedure and roles and exercise the plan.
Write criteria and severity levels that decide when an event is an incident.
Assess logged events and record the decision on each.
Respond under documented procedures covering containment, eradication, recovery and escalation.
Record the steps followed and close each incident.
Notify internal and external parties, including legal and contractual notification, within the required time.
Require a post-incident review for significant incidents.
Track resulting control improvements to completion.
Define how evidence of security events is identified, collected, acquired and preserved, including chain of custody.
Keep chain-of-custody or evidence-handling records where evidence was collected.
Plan how security controls are kept, or compensated, during a disruption.
Show that continuity tests or real disruptions considered and kept security requirements in place.
Define recovery time and recovery point objectives for critical IT services from an impact analysis.
Maintain recovery plans for the critical services.
Test the recovery plans, compare results with the objectives and act on gaps.
List every legal, regulatory and contractual requirement that bears on information security.
Record how each requirement is met, with an owner or control reference.
Review and update the list at least yearly and after relevant legal change.
Define how intellectual property is protected, including legitimate software sources and license compliance.
Reconcile software licenses against installed or subscribed software.
Define record types, retention periods and storage requirements reflecting legal and contractual needs.
Protect stored records from deletion, tampering and unauthorized access for the retention period.
Identify the privacy laws and contractual terms that apply to personal data processing.
Assign a person or role responsible for privacy and personal data protection.
Keep a current record of personal data processing for the scope.
Plan when security is independently reviewed and what triggers an unscheduled review.
Perform the independent review within the planned interval and report the results to management.
Assign managers or control owners to check compliance with policies and standards at a set frequency.
Perform compliance reviews and record non-compliances with actions.
Document operating procedures for key IT activities.
Make the current approved procedures available to those who need them.
Define the background checks required before a person joins.
Complete the checks before the start date or before access is granted.
State when re-screening is performed.
Scale the depth of checks to role, information accessed and risk.
Include security responsibilities of the individual and the organization in employment and contractor agreement templates.
Have current staff and contractors sign agreements containing those terms.
Define an awareness and training programme with content, audiences and frequency.
Have in-scope personnel complete awareness training within the set period and follow up non-completers.
Give technical and privileged roles role-specific training.
Update personnel when relevant policies or procedures change.
Document a disciplinary process that covers security policy violations.
Communicate the process to personnel.
Define the security responsibilities that continue after termination or change of employment.
Communicate the continuing obligations to leavers at exit.
Keep confidentiality agreement templates for staff and external parties reflecting protection needs.
Have staff, contractors and external parties with access sign the agreements.
Review the templates at the defined interval.
Set security requirements for working outside the premises.
Enforce the requirements technically for remote access.
Define and publish a channel for personnel to report security events.
Show that personnel report events through the channel in a timely way.
Tell personnel what to report and how.
Define physical perimeters for each in-scope site with the protection each needs.
Confirm the perimeters exist as described.
Record where no own premises are in scope and rely on provider assurance for hosting.
Define entry controls and who may enter each secure area.
Record visitors and escort them where required.
Review physical access rights and deactivate leavers' badges.
Specify physical security measures for offices, rooms and facilities.
Confirm the measures are in place for rooms holding sensitive information or equipment.
Define monitoring for unauthorized physical access and who responds.
Keep monitoring systems operational throughout the period.
Assess physical and environmental threats for each in-scope site.
Install and maintain the protection the assessment identifies.
Document rules for working in secure areas.
Make authorized personnel aware of the rules.
Set clear desk and clear screen rules for papers, removable media and unattended screens.
Enforce automatic screen lock after inactivity by configuration.
Check compliance with the rules and follow up findings.
Define siting requirements for equipment.
Confirm sampled equipment locations meet the requirements.
Document rules for protecting assets taken off premises.
Protect portable devices used off-site with full-disk encryption and remote wipe.
Define how storage media are acquired, used, transported and stored according to classification.
Restrict or encrypt removable media on endpoints in line with the procedure.
Record media disposals, for example with destruction certificates.
Define protection against power and other utility failures for critical facilities.
Keep maintenance and test records for UPS, generators or equivalents.
Define protection requirements for cabling.
Confirm sampled cabling and communications rooms meet the requirements.
Define maintenance requirements and schedules for in-scope equipment.
Have maintenance performed only by authorized personnel.
Clear or protect sensitive information on equipment before it is sent off site for repair.
Require data and licensed software to be removed or overwritten before equipment is disposed of or reused.
Keep verified wipe or destruction records for disposed or reissued devices.
Set security requirements for user endpoint devices.
Verify devices meet the required settings.
Authorize privileged access separately, limit it to those who need it and hold it in separate accounts.
Keep a current list of privileged accounts, each with a recorded authorization.
Review privileged access and remove unneeded rights.
Configure access controls in each system by role or group in line with the access rules.
Test that sampled users cannot reach information or functions outside their role.
Define who may read and write source code repositories, build tools and libraries.
Limit write access to authorized developers and require review before merge.
Set authentication strength by system sensitivity, including multi-factor where needed.
Enforce the required methods in the identity provider or systems.
Configure log-on protections such as lockout after failed attempts.
Define capacity requirements and thresholds for critical systems.
Monitor resource use and adjust capacity when thresholds are approached.
Define the malware protection required for each system type.
Keep protection installed, active and current on in-scope systems.
Deliver awareness material on malware risks such as phishing and suspicious attachments.
Define sources of vulnerability information, how exposure is assessed and fix deadlines by severity.
Run vulnerability scans or equivalent assessments at the set frequency.
Fix critical and high findings within deadlines or record a risk acceptance.
Penetration test internet-facing systems within the last 12 months and track findings to closure.
Document secure configuration baselines for each in-scope technology type.
Monitor systems against the baselines and remediate drift.
Review the baselines within their review interval.
Define when information must be deleted from systems, devices and media and by what method.
Delete information on schedule and keep records, such as deletion logs.
Define which data must be masked, pseudonymized or anonymized and in which contexts.
Apply masking as the rules require in non-production, support screens and reports.
Identify the sensitive information to protect and the channels it could leak through.
Configure leakage prevention measures on those channels.
Review and act on leakage alerts.
Set a backup policy covering scope, frequency, retention, location and protection.
Run backups as the policy requires and investigate failures.
Perform and record restore tests at the set frequency.
Define availability requirements for critical systems and document the redundancy that meets them.
Test failover at least yearly or observe it in a real event.
Define which events are logged for each system type and how long logs are kept.
Produce the defined logs and forward them to central storage.
Protect logs from tampering and unauthorized access, including by administrators.
Analyze logs, through alert rules or periodic review, and record the review.
Define what monitoring covers, what is anomalous and who responds.
Triage alerts and pass those warranting it to the incident process.
Name the approved reference time sources for in-scope systems.
Configure systems to synchronize with the approved sources.
Identify utility programs that can override controls and limit their use to authorized people.
Log use of those utilities.
Define who may install software on operational systems, from which sources and with what approval.
Enforce installation restrictions technically on servers and endpoints.
Define how networks and network devices are secured and managed.
Keep an up-to-date network diagram of the in-scope environment.
Review firewall and security group rules and remove unneeded or permissive ones.
Document the security features, service levels and requirements of each network service used.
Monitor network services against the agreed levels.
Define network segments by trust level or function and the traffic allowed between them.
Enforce the segmentation in firewall, VLAN or security group settings.
Define which categories of external website are blocked and how access is managed.
Keep web filtering active for in-scope users, including remote users.
Define where encryption is required and which algorithms and key lengths are approved.
Configure encryption on data stores, endpoints and transport as the rules require.
Define key management rules covering generation, storage, distribution, rotation, revocation and destruction.
Hold keys in a controlled store and rotate them as the rules require.
Set security rules for each phase of the development life cycle.
Show releases completed the required security steps.
Require security requirements to be identified, specified and approved when applications are developed or acquired.
Keep a documented, approved set of requirements for sampled applications.
Document secure engineering principles and keep them current.
Apply the principles in design or architecture reviews.
Maintain a secure coding standard that applies to in-house and outsourced code.
Run code review or automated scanning on code changes and address findings before release.
Give developers secure coding training at least yearly.
Define the security tests required at each stage and acceptance criteria before go-live.
Keep test results and an acceptance sign-off before production release.
Set security requirements in outsourced development contracts.
Monitor and review the outsourced work and keep records.
Separate development, test and production environments with rules for promoting changes.
Limit developers' standing write access to production, or approve and log it.
Secure non-production environments to the level of the data they hold.
Define a change procedure covering recording, impact and risk assessment, authorization, testing, rollback and communication.
Authorize production changes before implementation and keep testing evidence.
Record emergency changes and review and approve them afterwards.
Set rules for selecting and using test data, requiring masking or authorization for production or personal data.
Authorize copies of production data to test and delete them after testing.
Require audit and assurance tests on operational systems to be planned and approved by responsible management.
Keep authorization or rules-of-engagement records for tests on live systems.
Determine the external and internal issues that matter to the organization's purpose and affect its security outcomes.
Decide whether climate change is a relevant issue.
Determine the interested parties that are relevant to the security program.
Determine the requirements of those parties, which can include legal, regulatory and contractual ones and, under the 2024 amendment, climate-related ones.
Decide which of those requirements the security program will address.
Determine the boundaries and applicability of the program, considering issues, requirements and dependencies.
Keep the scope as documented information.
Establish and implement the security management system, with the processes it needs and their interactions.
Maintain and continually improve the system.
Make sure the security policy and objectives are set and fit the organization's strategic direction.
Build security program requirements into business processes.
Make sure the resources the program needs are available.
Communicate the importance of effective security, direct and support people and promote continual improvement.
Make sure the program achieves its intended outcomes.
Support other managers in showing leadership in their own areas.
Set a top-level policy suited to the organization's purpose that frames objectives and commits to meeting requirements and improving.
Keep the policy as documented information, communicate it and make it available to interested parties.
Assign and communicate responsibilities and authorities for relevant security roles.
Assign responsibility for conformity of the program and for reporting its performance to top management.
Considering the context issues and interested-party requirements, determine the risks and opportunities that must be addressed to achieve outcomes, prevent undesired effects and improve.
Plan actions to address them and build the actions into program processes.
Plan how to evaluate whether the actions work.
Define and apply a risk assessment process with risk acceptance criteria and criteria for performing assessments.
Make sure repeated assessments give consistent, valid and comparable results.
Identify risks to confidentiality, integrity and availability within scope and assign risk owners.
Analyze likelihood and consequence and evaluate and prioritize risks against the criteria.
Keep documented information about the risk assessment process.
Select risk treatment options for the assessed risks.
Determine all controls needed to implement the chosen treatment options and compare them with Annex A to check none is missed.
Produce a statement of applicability listing the necessary controls, why each is included, whether each is implemented and why any Annex A control is excluded.
Formulate a risk treatment plan.
Get risk owner approval of the plan and acceptance of residual risk, and keep documented information.
Set measurable security objectives at relevant functions, consistent with policy, taking risk results into account, and monitor, communicate, update and document them.
Plan what will be done, with what resources, by whom, by when and how results are evaluated.
Carry out needed changes to the security management system in a planned way.
Determine and provide the resources needed to establish, run, maintain and improve the program.
Determine the competence needed by people who affect security performance.
Ensure those people are competent through education, training or experience.
Take action to gain missing competence and evaluate whether it worked.
Keep evidence of competence.
Make people aware of the security policy.
Make people aware of their contribution to the program and the benefit of better performance.
Make people aware of the consequences of not conforming.
Decide what internal and external security communication is needed, when, with whom and how.
Include the documented information the standard requires and the organization judges necessary.
When creating or updating documents, set identification, format, review and approval.
Control documents so they are available, protected, distributed, stored, version controlled, retained and disposed of.
Identify and control documents of external origin that the program needs.
Plan, implement and control the processes needed to meet security requirements and carry out the planned actions, setting criteria for the processes.
Keep documented information giving confidence that processes ran as planned.
Control planned changes and review the effect of unintended changes.
Make sure externally provided processes, products or services that matter to the program are controlled.
Perform risk assessments at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed or occur.
Keep the results of the assessments.
Implement the risk treatment plan.
Keep the results of the treatment.
Determine what to monitor and measure, and the methods, which must give valid, comparable and reproducible results.
Determine when monitoring is done, when results are analyzed, and who does each; then evaluate security performance and the effectiveness of the program.
Keep evidence of the results.
Conduct internal audits at planned intervals to show whether the program meets the organization's own requirements and the standard's and is effectively implemented and maintained.
Plan and run an audit program covering frequency, methods, responsibilities, planning and reporting, taking account of how important the processes are and past audit results.
Define audit criteria and scope and choose auditors who are objective and impartial.
Report audit results to relevant management and keep evidence.
Have top management review the program at planned intervals.

Cover in the review the status of past actions, changes in issues and in interested-party needs, performance trends (nonconformities, measurements, audits, objectives), feedback from interested parties, risk results and treatment status, and improvement opportunities.
Record decisions on improvement and needed changes and keep evidence.
Continually improve the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the program.
React to a nonconformity by controlling and correcting it and dealing with the consequences.
Evaluate the need to remove causes, act, review the effectiveness of the action and change the program if needed.
Keep evidence of the nonconformities and the actions taken.
